comparator.name: Economics
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted TiSEM 2026–2027 EER v4 pp.69–70 explicitly labels the September-2026 cohort through 2028–2029. Years one and two each have sixty credits. First-listed mobility option is exchange: thirty approved non-overlapping bachelor credits in English, at least twenty-four in business/economics, excluding language and skills subjects. Host/package remain genuinely open within these restrictions. The first two adopted Spring elective entries are Competition Policy and Regulation and Environmental Economics, six credits each; other menu courses are not added. Third-year Spring is those twelve credits plus six Philosophy and History of Economic Thought and twelve thesis. The thesis requires 120 EC from semester six or 138 from semester seven, with first-year skills completed and timely registration/proposal approval. The example completes 150 EC including R/Python skills before Spring thesis. Zero-credit GROW is extracurricular. Stale 2018 assessment dates inside the current Philosophy/Science/Free-Markets catalogue text are not represented as current scheduling facts.

components.name: The Political Economy of Big Data
Approved Economics and Business Exchange
components.note: This example uses the 30-EC exchange option. At least 24 EC must be in business or economics. All courses must be bachelor-level, taught in English, approved in advance and non-overlapping with the home programme; language and skills courses cannot count. The host and approved course package remain open. Internship-plus-elective and minor routes are alternatives, not extra credits.

components.name: Philosophy and History of Economic Thought
Competition Policy and Regulation
components.note: First selected six-credit elective from the published Spring list. It uses economic models and Python to examine agreements, dominance, mergers and sectoral regulation. Microeconomics, mathematics and Industrial Economics are completed earlier.

components.name: Environmental Economics
components.note: Second selected six-credit elective from the published Spring list. It studies externalities, environmental instruments, valuation, resource management and climate policy.

components.name: BSc Thesis Economics
components.note: The twelve-credit thesis is independent economic research, written and presented in English. Entry in semester six requires at least 120 completed EC and passed first-year skills requirements; semester seven or later requires 138 EC. This example completes 150 EC before starting. Timely registration and approval of the research proposal are required. A failed attempt cannot be followed by an immediate next-semester restart.

basisLabels: Public policy, institutions, development and inequality
courseTraceability.rationale: Introduction to Economics Directly supplies Introduces microeconomic principles and short-run macroeconomic analysis. The microeconomic component examines supply and demand, strategic interaction, consumer choice, production, costs and competitive markets. The macroeconomic component introduces output, unemployment and inflation, then relates goods and financial markets through the IS-LM model. Students use algebra and graphs to explain economic behaviour and apply models to economic issues.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Public policy, institutions, development and inequality”.

basisLabels: Finance, investment, banking and accounting for economists
courseTraceability.rationale: Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations complements financial decisions through venture funding, finance/operations planning and business-model appraisal; supplies the formal prerequisite for banking. It implements the explicit academic basis “Finance, investment, banking and accounting for economists”.

basisLabels: Finance, investment, banking and accounting for economists
courseTraceability.rationale: Accounting & Corporate Finance Directly supplies Introduces financial accounting, management accounting and investment appraisal, including accounting's social role and accountability implications. Students record transactions, prepare and interpret financial statements, and analyze performance and financing. The course then examines costing, pricing, budgeting, organizational control and sustainable management accounting. Investment decisions are evaluated using accounting and discounted-cash-flow measures. A case study analyzes the misuse of an accounting principle and its financial-statement effects.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Finance, investment, banking and accounting for economists”.

Political economy of data, industrial economics and economic power
courseTraceability.rationale: Introduction to Programming Directly supplies Introduces computational problem-solving and programming in Python. Students develop structured programs using branching, iteration, functions and data collections, then progress to recursion, exception handling and object-oriented programming with inheritance. Elements of logic, sets and enumeration support computational reasoning. Exercises and projects require students to write, trace, test, debug and explain programs that solve problems of moderate complexity.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Mathematics, statistics, programming, econometrics and economic data analysis” and “Political economy of data, industrial economics and economic power”.

basisLabels: Public economics, development, inequality, institutions and economic policy
courseTraceability.rationale: Research Methods & Statistics Directly supplies Introduces empirical research design and statistical analysis, followed by a substantial student research project. Students study operationalization, measurement quality, sampling, surveys and experimental and nonexperimental designs, then descriptive statistics, estimation, hypothesis testing and introductory regression. R and R Commander support data display and analysis. Project teams develop instruments and a research plan, collect and analyze data, and report results under explicit research-ethics and privacy requirements.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Public economics, development, inequality, institutions and economic policy”.

basisLabels: Mathematics, statistics, programming, econometrics and economic data analysis
Political economy of data, industrial economics and economic power
courseTraceability.rationale: Ethics Directly supplies Studies moral reasoning through historical and contemporary ethical theories and close philosophical reading. Utilitarianism, consequentialism, Kantian ethics, virtue ethics, contractarianism and feminist ethics lead into Nietzsche's genealogy, Murdoch's account of goodness and Nagel's treatments of value, perspective, death and meaning. Reflection and research essays require interpretation, argument evaluation and an independent position on ethical theory or a practical ethical problem.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Mathematics, statistics, programming, econometrics and economic data analysis” and “Political economy of data, industrial economics and economic power”.

basisLabels: Mathematics, statistics, programming, econometrics and economic data analysis
courseTraceability.rationale: Mathematical Methods Directly supplies Develops single-variable calculus and related mathematical tools for modelling scientific problems. Functions, limits and differentiation lead to optimization, Taylor series, complex numbers, integration and differential equations. Students solve problems analytically and with Mathematica, including numerical approximation. A project implements, analyzes and adapts a dynamic model, requiring interpretation of its behaviour and explanation of the computational results.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Mathematics, statistics, programming, econometrics and economic data analysis”.

basisLabels: Macroeconomics, international finance and trade, business cycles and growth
courseTraceability.rationale: International Macroeconomics Directly supplies Examines short-, medium- and long-run macroeconomic dynamics and policy, including international dimensions. Students study goods, financial and labour markets, inflation and unemployment, economic growth, expectations and the open economy. IS-LM and IS-LM-PC models connect markets and policy effects. Algebraic and graphical analysis and interpretation of macroeconomic indicators support the evaluation of economic developments and fiscal and monetary policy.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Macroeconomics, international finance and trade, business cycles and growth”.

basisLabels: Public policy, institutions, development and inequality
Mathematics, statistics, programming, econometrics and economic data analysis
courseTraceability.rationale: Statistics & Experimental Methods Directly supplies Develops experimental-design knowledge and practical statistical analysis for health and behavioural research. Students choose, fit, diagnose and interpret multivariable models, comparing means, analyzing categorical outcomes and studying latent constructs. R, primarily through R Commander, supports repeated practical exercises; SPSS is an optional alternative. Data-analysis papers and a poster connect research questions and hypotheses to appropriate models, assumption checks, substantive interpretation and APA reporting.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Public policy, institutions, development and inequality” and “Mathematics, statistics, programming, econometrics and economic data analysis”.

basisLabels: Mathematics, statistics, programming, econometrics and economic data analysis
courseTraceability.rationale: Probability & Statistics Directly supplies Provides a rigorous introduction to probability and mathematical statistics, from probability spaces and random variables to multivariate distributions and statistical inference. Students study estimation, confidence intervals, hypothesis tests and maximum-likelihood methods, followed by an introduction to Bayesian reasoning. Mathematica simulations verify analytical results. A substantial project implements and compares random-sampling algorithms, including inverse sampling, accept-reject sampling and Gibbs sampling.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Mathematics, statistics, programming, econometrics and economic data analysis”.

basisLabels: Political economy of data, industrial economics and economic power
courseTraceability.rationale: Business & Economy in the Age of AI Directly supplies Examines AI's business, economic and societal implications without requiring a technical background. AI foundations and limitations lead into applications across enterprise functions and industries, labour-market change, productivity, innovation, market structure and inequality. Governance, corporate responsibility, regulation and future scenarios connect technological developments to institutional choices. Students analyze business cases and competing scholarly arguments, then investigate a country's AI readiness, workforce, regulation and industrial policy.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Political economy of data, industrial economics and economic power”.

courseTraceability.rationale: Introduction to Data Science Directly supplies Introduces data analysis and visualization in R through practical work with tabular, textual and spatial data. Students import, clean, transform and join data, explore patterns, and construct visualizations using tidy-data principles and the grammar of graphics. Web scraping and basic programming functions extend the workflow. A student research project applies these tools to a question using data from a field of interest.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Mathematics, statistics, programming, econometrics and economic data analysis” and “Political economy of data, industrial economics and economic power”.

Students examine choice under uncertainty, non-egoistic preferences and cognitive limitations, then monopoly, strategic behaviour and labour and capital markets. basisLabels: Mathematics, statistics, programming, econometrics and economic data analysis
courseTraceability.rationale: Linear Algebra Directly supplies Develops linear algebra from systems of equations and matrix operations to vector spaces, linear transformations, eigenvalues and orthogonality. Students study least-squares approximation, symmetric matrices, quadratic forms and singular value decomposition. Applications include discrete signals, difference equations, Markov chains, dynamical systems, graphics and principal component analysis. Mathematica exercises teach computer-algebra approaches to larger problems alongside analytical problem-solving.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Mathematics, statistics, programming, econometrics and economic data analysis”.

courseTraceability.rationale: International Business & Governance Directly supplies Examines how international trade, globalization and political, sociocultural and technological forces shape firms' cross-border decisions. Economic foundations include trade theories, foreign direct investment, foreign exchange and the monetary system. Students analyze governance, responsibility and trade-policy conflicts, investigate an international-business question, and develop an evidence-based market-entry strategy covering country attractiveness and business functions. A tariff case applies game theory to stakeholder choices and negotiation.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Finance, investment, banking and accounting for economists” and “Political economy of data, industrial economics and economic power”.

courseTraceability.rationale: Machine Learning Directly supplies Introduces statistical learning for understanding data and predicting outcomes. Students study regression and classification, model accuracy, resampling, regularization, nonlinear models, trees, support vector machines and unsupervised learning. Practical assignments evaluate methods on real data using R or Python. Projects emphasize informative predictor construction, test-set prediction, appropriate model choice and clear reporting of results and limitations.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Mathematics, statistics, programming, econometrics and economic data analysis” and “Political economy of data, industrial economics and economic power”.

courseTraceability.rationale: Behavioral Economics Directly supplies This course integrates insights from psychology into economic theory to better understand how people make decisions. Learn how actual behavior deviates from the predictions of traditional economic models due to biases, heuristics, and framing. Through experiments, students will deepen their understanding of decision-making and its implications for economic theory and practice.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Microeconomics, welfare, strategic behaviour, competition and market regulation”.

basisLabels: Mathematics, statistics, programming, econometrics and economic data analysis
courseTraceability.rationale: Econometrics Directly supplies Econometrics supplies tools to analyze data to answer questions of causality and prediction. In this course you learn three estimators—Ordinary Least Squares, Generalized Least Squares, and Instrumental Variables—and three tests—t-test, F-test, and LM-test. Understanding the basic rules of econometrics, particularly the sampling distribution concept, is key, and the course uses Monte Carlo simulations in Stata to visualize it. Tools are applied to estimate economic relationships and make predictions, and students write an empirical paper.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Mathematics, statistics, programming, econometrics and economic data analysis”.

basisLabels: Mathematics, statistics, programming, econometrics and economic data analysis
Finance, investment, banking and accounting for economists
courseTraceability.rationale: Market Research complements empirical firm/consumer inquiry with planning and conducting customer research, analysing findings and presenting business recommendations; no unsupported named techniques. It implements the explicit academic basis “Mathematics, statistics, programming, econometrics and economic data analysis” and “Finance, investment, banking and accounting for economists”.

basisLabels: Finance, investment, banking and accounting for economists
courseTraceability.rationale: Money, Banking & Finance Directly supplies Examines financial markets and institutions, including the pricing of bonds, stocks and derivatives, interest rates and their risk and term structure, commercial-bank balance sheets and performance, financial structure and regulation, banking fragility and financial crises, central banks, money creation and monetary policy. Students apply algebraic and graphical analysis to financial and monetary problems. In the Stanford Banking Game they manage a simulated bank, analyse performance in Excel dashboards, forecast financial statements, and make evidence-based decisions about loans, deposits, capital, liquidity and risk. A small research project extends a selected financial or monetary research article through additional literature, a case study or updated evidence.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Finance, investment, banking and accounting for economists”.

An individual analysis applies a course concept to contemporary social life without original data collection. A group paper develops a sociological question and analyzes a social problem using theory and academic literature.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Public policy, institutions, development and inequality” and “How do markets, institutions and public policy shape growth, inequality and broad prosperity?”.

Students apply governance frameworks to a Zeeland issue, consult relevant organizations or experts, and produce policy advice or an evaluation assessing effectiveness, feasibility and stakeholder interests.. Students develop a project plan, code amendments, assess salience and trace legislative processes.. The microeconomic component examines supply and demand, strategic interaction, consumer choice, production, costs and competitive markets. The macroeconomic component introduces output, unemployment and inflation, then relates goods and financial markets through the IS-LM model. Students use algebra and graphs to explain economic behaviour and apply models to economic issues.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Public policy, institutions, development and inequality”.

Students record transactions, prepare and interpret financial statements, and analyze performance and financing. The course then examines costing, pricing, budgeting, organizational control and sustainable management accounting. Investment decisions are evaluated using accounting and discounted-cash-flow measures. A case study analyzes the misuse of an accounting principle and its financial-statement effects.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Finance, investment, banking and accounting for economists”.

Exercises and projects require students to write, trace, test, debug and explain programs that solve problems of moderate complexity.. courseTraceability.rationale: Ethics Directly supplies Studies moral reasoning through historical and contemporary ethical theories and close philosophical reading. Reflection and research essays require interpretation, argument evaluation and an independent position on ethical theory or a practical ethical problem.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Mathematics, statistics, programming, econometrics and economic data analysis” and “Political economy of data, industrial economics and economic power”.

Algebraic and graphical analysis and interpretation of macroeconomic indicators support the evaluation of economic developments and fiscal and monetary policy.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Macroeconomics, international finance and trade, business cycles and growth”.

Governance, corporate responsibility, regulation and future scenarios connect technological developments to institutional choices. Students analyze business cases and competing scholarly arguments, then investigate a country's AI readiness, workforce, regulation and industrial policy.. It implements the explicit academic basis “Political economy of data, industrial economics and economic power”.

It implements the explicit academic basis “Microeconomics, welfare, strategic behaviour, competition and market regulation”.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest curriculum covers the programme-wide microeconomic, macroeconomic and quantitative core. Public economics/institutions/inequality and financial economics each support coherent, mechanically feasible and substantially distinct UCR alternatives. Behavioral and experimental economics is a further evidenced direction, but no fourth alternative can be included.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both develop reflective competence assessment, study/career choices and development actions. UCR also includes writing, source research and civic collaboration.
Both study financial statements, accounting techniques, costs and organisational control. UCR additionally includes corporate investment appraisal.

Both examine economic power, market structure and societal risks in data/AI economies. Tilburg specifically models data intermediaries, political participation and belief formation; UCR spans enterprise, labour and industrial-policy effects.

Both analyse financial contracts, pricing and investment risk. Tilburg adds dedicated capital-budgeting/CAPM/cost-of-capital foundations; UCR also centres banks, monetary policy and institutional risks.
Both use models of consumers, firms and competitive or imperfect markets. UCR also introduces macroeconomics; the course is counted only once.

Both examine open-economy models, international financial relationships and macroeconomic policy. Tilburg centres exchange-rate theories and monetary systems; UCR spans additional short- and long-run macroeconomic questions.
Both study imperfect competition, strategic firm behaviour, market power and efficiency. Tilburg gives a more dedicated oligopoly, entry, vertical-contract and innovation model sequence.
Both evaluate government intervention, redistribution, public goods and economic policy with models and evidence. Their selected empirical applications differ.

Both develop regression and instrumental-variable estimation for empirical economic research. UCR uses Stata, GLS and Monte Carlo illustration; Tilburg uses R and prepares for time-series/panel methods.

Both study trade theories, cross-border economic relationships and trade-policy conflicts. Tilburg develops calibrated quantitative trade models; UCR applies trade and governance reasoning to international firm decisions.

Both import, manipulate and visualise data in R and use programming functions. Tilburg additionally centres numerical optimisation and economic/stochastic simulation; UCR develops empirical data workflows.

Both develop Python programs, data structures, control flow and analytical problem solving. Tilburg has a shorter economic simulation/data focus; UCR also develops recursion and object-oriented programming.
Both develop calculus and mathematical techniques for modelling and optimisation. Tilburg applies these to economics; UCR includes differential-equation and scientific dynamic-model work.

Both study probability distributions, estimation, confidence intervals and tests. UCR develops more mathematical and Bayesian/simulation methods; Tilburg centres economic applications and Excel/basic R.

Both analyse environmental policy instruments, actors and institutional implementation. UCR centres governance, participation and policy advice; Tilburg adds resource-allocation models, valuation and dynamic environmental economics.

Both develop normative arguments about justice and responsible choices. Tilburg explicitly combines distributive justice and markets with reasoning errors and scientific method; UCR studies a wider range of ethical theories.
